name: UWL World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own served title-history page runs a fully dated chain of fifteen reigns across fourteen holders, from Masked Menace's founding reign (11 January 1997) through Chris Jericho's win on 29 October 1999 — Black Shadow alone holding it twice, in April and again from July to September 1997 — mixing original characters (Moonbeam Kid, Trasher, Big Daddy Cool Zader, Punishing One) with real-wrestler names and gimmicks (Bret Hart, Tommy Dreamer, Chris Jericho). The fed's own Summer Blast '99 results page corroborates one link in the chain from the other side — Psycho defending against Punishing One that night — though its own text breaks off before showing the finish the title ledger independently records. The ledger's own last entry records the title vacant from 1 January 2000, with no further champion attested.

name: UWL Tag-Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own Summer Blast '99 results page shows the Double "A" Express retaining this belt twice in one night — against Shawn Michaels & Triple H, then against Pink & Phoenix (billed the same night as "The Bash Brothers") — under two different names for the same title, "UWL Tag-Team" and "UWL World Tag-Team," the fed's own text never explaining the difference. No earlier or later UWL document survives naming when the reign began or how it ended.

name: UWL United States Championship
epitaph: The fed's own Summer Blast '99 results page shows Frost pinning Stone Cold Steve Austin with the Frostbite to win this belt on 20 June 1999. No earlier document survives naming when Austin's own reign began, and no later document survives naming how Frost's reign ended.

name: UWL Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The fed's own rules page mandates that this belt always be defended in a Falls Count Anywhere, No DQ, hardcore/weapons match; its Summer Blast '99 results page shows Chris Jericho retaining it against Rebel Rouser with a power bomb, the pair brawling through the whole arena. No earlier or later UWL document survives naming when the reign began or how it ended.

name: UWL Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own rules page caps this division at 230 lbs. and under; its Summer Blast '99 results page shows Chris Jericho retaining the belt against Stevie P. with a superplex. No earlier or later UWL document survives naming when the reign began or how it ended.

name: UWL Television Championship
epitaph: The fed's own Summer Blast '99 results page shows Ripper retaining this belt against Johnny Hays, submitting him to the Ripp Gripp. No earlier or later UWL document survives naming when the reign began or how it ended.
